Severity
Palette
More options
Threshold
How it works

The colours are the fills and strokes the objects show (classes and inherited colours included); gradients, patterns and pictures are not measured, though the view shows them. Each pair is compared with CIEDE2000 after simulating the red, green and blue cone deficiencies at every severity from 10 % to 100 % (Machado et al. 2009); a pair that normal vision tells apart but some severity brings under the threshold is listed with the mildest severity where it happens, since most colour-blind readers are only mildly affected. Remapping gives each colour, most used first, its own palette colour, first avoiding pairs that run together at mild severities, then staying close to the original colours, and keeps greys, black and white. Click a colour to select what uses it. One undo step.

How it works

Nothing is read from the file: PNG and JPEG keep no microscope calibration, and their dpi is for printing. Take the pixel size from the microscope software or ImageJ (Image › Properties). The bar's length comes from it and the picture's size on the page, and is redrawn whenever the picture changes; a rotated picture needs square pixels.

  1. Select a picture
  2. Click Add zoom inset
  3. Drag the box on the picture to choose the region

Region
Size
px
Zoom Box
More options
How it works

The region is kept in the picture's own pixels, so it stays on the same spot as the picture moves or scales; drag or resize the box (or crop the inset) to change it. The inset shows the embedded picture's own pixels, not a screenshot. The same region on other pictures is the same relative place in each, not an alignment of them.

  1. Select the pictures; crop one of them first with C, or type the region
  2. Check the region; the outlines preview it on each picture
  3. Click Crop all

Region
Size
px
More options
How it works

The region is in the original picture's pixels, taken from the first selected picture that has a crop, so it lands on the same pixels of every picture however each is placed or scaled. Like the crop tool, it only clips: the pixels are never changed, and C still adjusts one picture alone. One undo step for all.

  1. Select pictures
  2. Adjust
  3. Click Apply
Levels
Gamma Brightness Contrast
More options
Curve

Click to add a point, drag to move it, double-click to remove it.

How it works

The adjustment is an SVG filter on the picture (one lookup table per channel, ahead of any tint from Channels), so the pixels never change and Inkscape shows it too. Black and White are the same values as Min and Max under Channels. Gamma and curves are not linear: say so in the figure legend or methods when you submit.

  1. Select grayscale pictures
  2. Pick a colour and click Tint
  3. Or select 2–7 pictures and click Merge

Colour
More options
Range
Merge channels

Select 2 to 7 pictures of the same pixel size, in the order of their channels.

Blend
How it works

For showing, not for measuring: the colour and range are an SVG filter (the range, which is Adjust picture's Black and White, then grey by Rec. 709 weights, then the colour), and the pictures' pixels are never changed. Levels are those of the embedded 8-bit picture. Merging needs pictures of the same pixel size; they are overlaid pixel to pixel as they are, not registered, in a new group beside them.

NameCategory

svguest: I once paid for Adobe, then fell for open-source Inkscape, but at heart I've always loved lightweight tools, ideally ones that run right in the browser; now that AI is here, we can hand-craft the manual parts of our workflows exactly the way we want.

To start, add an API key for GLM or DeepSeek. Keys are kept in this browser; Models and keys shows how each service connects.

Context

What the AI read for the last reply: the whole chat goes with each message, other chats don't. Near the model's limit, the chat is summarised and continues in a new one that still edits the same figure.

Help

Getting started

  1. Open a figure. Ctrl+O, or drop an SVG from ggplot2, Inkscape or Illustrator onto the canvas. File › New starts a blank page.
  2. Select. Click a part; Ctrl+click takes its whole group; drag on an empty spot to box select.
  3. Edit. Drag to move, pull the handles to scale or rotate, double-click a text to retype it. The Properties panel on the right sets exact sizes, colours and fonts.
  4. Lay out. The FigKit menu sizes, aligns and labels panels, and adds scale bars and zoom insets.
  5. Save. Ctrl+S exports the SVG; the File menu also exports PDF, PNG and JPG.

Can't find a command? Ctrl+K searches all of them. Every change can be undone with Ctrl+Z.

Layout

Move sections
Drag a section by the dotted grip at the left of its title: drop it between two sections, on the other column or on the canvas. The arrangement is kept in this browser; View › Reset layout puts everything back.
Float a section
The window button at the right of a section's title lifts it out as a floating window: drag it by its title, resize it from the bottom-right corner. Click the button again to dock it back.
Right-click a title
Float, dock left or right, collapse, hide; Show only when it applies, for floating sections. View › Layout has presets, Blocks, Lock layout, Export and Import

Draw

V T
Select (also Esc); text: click to type or to edit
M L \
Rectangle, ellipse, line; Shift: square, circle, 45°
A B
Arrow, inhibition (blunt end), in one button with the line; ends snap to objects' points and outlines (Ctrl: off) and stay attached as the objects move; moving the arrow itself detaches it; Heads and Scale in Appearance set each end
W E {
Wedge (drag from the thin end), elbow connector (attaches like an arrow; its diamond moves the middle), brace (drag along what it groups: left to right points up)
Enter
More shapes (flowchart, block arrows, symbols, UML), in the grid button under the ellipse: drag to draw; double-click one, or a rectangle or an ellipse, to type inside it (any other closed shape: select it and press Enter; point editing: click a corner handle). Triangle and diamond line heads are under Heads in Properties. The text stays centred on its shape; click it once more to select the text itself
I
Eyedropper: click an object to give the selection its style; Alt+click gives an object the picked style
C
Crop a photo: click it, drag the handles; Enter applies, Esc cancels
Colours
Every colour field opens the same picker: drag the square and the hue bar, or type or paste a code (#2F6DB5, rgb(47, 109, 181), a colour name); a pasted code applies at once and the copy button copies the HEX code. Its swatches are the figure's colours, recent ones and palettes (My palette is FigKit › Colours' palette); its eyedropper picks colours from the figure and its pictures in any modern browser; the screen button also picks outside the page where supported
Swatches
Fill and stroke of the selection, or of new shapes; Shift+X swaps, D sets none and black, / removes the one in front

SVG Chat

Model
Beside Send: the model that draws, its thinking, and which model reads images (Auto: the drawing model when it can, else one that can)
Models and keys
Your GLM or DeepSeek API key, tested when entered; TBtools' model needs none
Enter
Send; Shift+Enter new line
Chats
svguest opens on a new chat; the title switches to an earlier one, renames or deletes it; each is kept in this browser (Kept in this browser… saves them as files) and the AI reads only the current one; near the model's context limit a chat is summarised and continues in a new one
Attach
An image to redraw or a text file to draw from (or paste, drop)
Selection
Select objects first to ask about them or have them changed in place
Retry
Under the latest drawing: ask again, with this model or another
Long replies
Cut off at the token limit, they continue automatically, up to 3 times
Waiting
A seconds counter shows it is working; Stop cancels

File

Tabs
Each file opens in its own tab at the top, with its own undo history; + starts a new canvas, × or a middle-click closes a tab
Ctrl+O
Open an SVG; a PNG or JPG is placed
PDF and .ai
Open or drop a PDF or PDF-compatible .ai. Click pages in Pages to edit within one document; switching keeps each page and its last three undo steps for this session. Open selected in tabs creates linked page tabs. Export document saves a multi-page PDF or one SVG per page in a ZIP. Import places one page into the current canvas. CMYK becomes sRGB through the file's colour profile, or Coated FOGRA39 when none is present
CorelDRAW
A .cdr can't be read: export a PDF or SVG from CorelDRAW first, or open it in Inkscape and save it as SVG
Open recent
The last 10 files as you left them, copied into this browser as you work (File › Auto-save turns it off; Auto-save to a folder, in Chrome or Edge, also writes them into a folder you pick); Kept in this browser… saves the copies as files
Ctrl+Shift+P
Import into this canvas (also Ctrl+I)
Ctrl+S
Export SVG, later to the same file; Ctrl+Shift+S to a new one. In a PDF/AI document, open Export document instead
Ctrl+P
Vector PDF through the print dialog (best in Chrome or Edge)
Drop a file
An SVG opens or is imported; an image is placed
File menu
New; PNG or JPG at 300 or 600 dpi on white, with the dpi stored (JPG at top quality)

FigKit

Size each
Give every selected object the same width or height, in proportion or stretched
Grid, align, space
Columns and gaps; edges or centres; the same gap, equal gaps or a total length; outlined before anything moves
Positions
Record where objects sit and put others there; swap two
Labels, frames
A, B, C… and rectangles that follow their panels; run again to update them
Scale bar
From the pixel size you enter; redrawn when the picture changes
Zoom inset
A box on a picture and its region enlarged; drag the box to change it
Batch crop
Crop one picture, select the others of the same size: Crop all gives each the same pixels
Adjust picture
Levels, gamma, brightness, contrast and curves over the picture's histogram, previewed until Apply; the pixels are unchanged
Pseudocolor
Tint grayscale pictures (Min and Max are Adjust's Black and White); merge 2 to 7 channels
Colour blindness
Colours that run together for colour-blind readers, the canvas as they see it, and a remap to a safe palette

Library

Add
Select objects, then Add selection in the Library (or Right-click › Add to Library…); give it a name and a category
Insert
Click an asset to put it at the centre of the view, or drag it onto the canvas; it keeps its size in mm
Keep a copy
The Library lives in this browser: Export .zip now and then (it reminds you), Import… takes it back here or in another browser

On a Mac, ⌘ works in place of Ctrl. Everything runs in your browser; only what you send to SVG Chat leaves it.

    Release notes

    Kept in this browser

    Copies svguest keeps for you between visits, in this browser only.

    Open recent
    SVG Chat
    Library
    • They sit in this site's own storage in the browser (IndexedDB: sgDocs, sgChats, sgLib), not in a folder: a web page can't write to your disk by itself.
    • Download .zip saves the SVG copies, or each chat as a web page with its figures.
    • Each browser, private window, TBtools and downloaded copy of svguest keeps its own; clearing this site's data deletes them.
    • File › Auto-save turns the copies on or off; in Chrome or Edge, File › Auto-save to a folder also writes the open file into a folder you pick.

    Choose pages

    Original files and editing drafts stay in this session. Refreshing clears them.
    Export document

    Unchanged pages keep their original PDF content. Edited pages become high-resolution images; their text is no longer searchable and original annotations are omitted. Use SVG ZIP to keep editable vectors.

    One editable SVG per page, with page-numbered filenames. Original PDF annotations and unsupported PDF features are not included.
